name: bencher
description: Catch performance regressions before they merge

interface.longDescription:
Bencher is a continuous benchmarking platform. It stores benchmark results from CI and local runs, tracks them over time, and raises an alert when a result crosses a threshold.

This plugin connects to Bencher Cloud through the Bencher MCP server and includes a skill on using Bencher and the bencher CLI.

The MCP tools list and view projects, branches, testbeds, benchmarks, measures, thresholds, alerts, reports, plots, and bare metal runner jobs, and view a single metric. They query performance data over time and render a performance plot as an image. They create branches, testbeds, benchmarks, measures, thresholds, and reports, and update branches, testbeds, benchmarks, measures, thresholds, and alerts. They submit a run: raw benchmark harness output that Bencher parses into a report.

Public projects are readable without signing in. Sign in with a Bencher account to read private projects and to change them. Every tool acts with your project roles. The plugin has no tools that delete anything.
defaultPrompt: Run my benchmarks on Bencher bare metal and show me the results.
Compare my branch to main on Bencher bare metal and flag regressions.
Run my benchmarks on Bencher bare metal in GitHub Actions on every pull request.

positive.description: Find a public project by name
positive.prompt: Find the public project named Bencher on Bencher.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the matching public projects, including Bencher (slug bencher).

positive.prompt: Show the details of the bencher project on Bencher.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the Bencher project: name Bencher, slug bencher, public visibility, and its repository URL https://github.com/bencherdev/bencher.

positive.prompt: Show the latest alerts for the bencher project on Bencher.
positive.expected_behavior: List the project's most recent alerts with the benchmark, status, and the threshold limit each one crossed.

positive.prompt: Show the Latency of the Adapter::Json benchmark on the devel branch and intel-v1 testbed of the bencher project on Bencher over the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Look up the branch, testbed, benchmark, and measure, then return the Latency value of each run in the last 30 days with its date.

positive.prompt: Plot the Latency of the Adapter::Json benchmark on the devel branch and intel-v1 testbed of the bencher project on Bencher over the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Look up the branch, testbed, benchmark, and measure, then show a plot image of the Latency values over the last 30 days.
